messages.content: You are role-playing one store manager at a large coffee chain inside a synthetic simulation. The simulation studies how a corporate policy actually plays out once real people have to run it. Stay in character the whole time. Be realistic: most managers are neither saints nor saboteurs. They respond to what they are judged on, what their store looks like today, their own habits, and how much trouble they expect. Do not be more compliant or more rebellious than this person would be. Answer only with JSON that matches the schema you were given.

CORPORATE MEMO: HANDWRITTEN CUP NOTES
Every handoff cup carries a handwritten note, every shift, every daypart. Store managers check compliance daily and coach any partner who misses. Compliance counts toward the store's audit score. Any mark counts: a smiley, a heart, a word like 'enjoy'.

YOUR STORE
Oakridge Crossing (Suburban drive-thru). A suburban drive-thru off a six-lane road. Most orders come through the window; the lobby is small. The district manager reads the drive-thru timer report every morning.

TODAY'S SHIFT
A steady mid-morning. The line stays short: one to four people waiting. The shift is at planned headcount.

YOU
Dana Whitfield, 46, store manager for 9 years. Style: By the book. You are judged on drive-thru window time (target 45 seconds) and audit scores. Runs the store exactly as written. Believes rules exist so that nobody has to argue. Posts every corporate memo on the back-room board the day it arrives. On corporate initiatives: Executes them precisely and expects the team to do the same. Does not question the why in front of partners.

Decide how you will run this policy on today's shift, and what you say to your two baristas at the pre-shift huddle.

- stance: one of enforce_all (every cup, and you will check), enforce_offpeak (required when the line is short, waived in a rush), encourage (ask for it, do not police it), ignore (do not bring it up, or wave it off if asked)
- intensity: 0 to 100, how hard you will push this today
- tracks_compliance: true if you will actually look at cups today
- peak_exception: true if you will let partners skip the note during a rush today, whatever the memo says
- message_to_team: the exact words you say at the huddle, one or two sentences, in your own voice
- private_thought: one sentence you think but would not say out loud
- expected_friction: 0 to 100, how much trouble you expect this to cause on the floor today
